newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to remove stigma on illegitimate children.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to remove stigma on illegitimate children.

text.p: Sri Lankan children may not have to worry much longer about being stigmatised because their parents were not married when they were born, Health Minister Mohammed Fowzie said on Thursday.
After 39 years, the government plans to do away with the question, "Were parents married at time of birth?" in the birth certificate, Fowzie told Reuters.
"It just isn't fair. Children become illegitimate and are branded as bastards for absolutely no fault of their own," he told Reuters.
Fowzie said a large number of Sri Lankan parents, mostly in rural areas, still had children out of wedlock.
"Though they are not married, many of them lead very decent family lives. But their children's futures are clouded because of this one line in the birth certificate," he said.
Fowzie said he has submitted a proposal to the cabinet to do away with the question, which was introduced in the Sri Lankan birth certificate in 1958.
